raw_response:
Answer: A
Reason: In patients with pulmonary artery hypertension, chronic elevation of pulmonary pressures leads to right ventricular hypertrophy and dilation (cardiomegaly) and can cause weakening of the pulmonary arterial wall, predisposing to pseudoaneurysm formation; thus, the cardiomegaly is likely secondary to the long-standing PA hypertension that also contributed to the pseudoaneurysm.
